scopeClaim.statement: Assessment is limited to the single declared runnable obligation and the supplied fixed source crops; it makes no repository-wide or all-entry completeness claim.

results.explanation: The supplied collection name is bound at POST /process/text and, when present, is passed to the shared validator with access_type='write'. For a non-admin, an existing knowledge-base ID is added to the allowed set only if Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id succeeds; if that check fails and the knowledge base exists, the name is not added. The shared validator then raises HTTP 403 before save_docs_to_vector_db is called. Thus the source-visible authorization chain denies the stated non-admin/no-write-grant case, matching the accepted policy expectation and refuting the proposition that the principal can perform the protected write.

entry.statement: The declared entry is POST /process/text, implemented by process_text.

binding.statement: The entry binds the caller's supplied collection_name from form_data; when supplied, it is the value passed into collection-access validation.

The principal is a verified non-administrator, and the target is an existing knowledge-base collection for which the principal has no ownership or explicit write grant; the accepted requirement is to deny that write.

condition.statement: The relevant request condition is that the caller supplies an existing collection name and the principal is a verified non-admin without write permission.

For non-admins, an ordinary collection name that is an existing knowledge-base ID is checked using the requested access type; a name is allowed as a legacy or ephemeral collection only when no knowledge base exists for that ID.

control.statement: The caller invokes _validate_collection_access with access_type='write' for the supplied collection name.
The shared validator computes the allowed set, identifies denied requested names, and raises HTTP 403 when any requested collection is denied.

For a non-admin targeting an existing knowledge-base ID without a successful write-access check, the ID is not added to the allowed set: the code adds it only when check_access_by_user_id succeeds, while the fallback allows only when get_knowledge_by_id finds no knowledge base.

effect.statement: The protected effect would be saving a document containing the attacker-selected form_data.content to the selected collection through save_docs_to_vector_db.
Because the validator raises 403 for the denied collection, the protected save call is not reached in the stated case.
